# Eight-channel sensor batch reducer

Improve the reducer used by a vibration monitor. It reports the sum of all overlapping window means for every channel in a captured batch. Every window and sample contributes to the report; the operator cannot drop samples when the machine is busy. The supported CLI is `./probe N WINDOW`, with `1 <= WINDOW <= N <= 600000` and eight finite outputs. `python3 public_check.py` builds and probes the starter. Output tolerance is `max(0.02, 2e-7 * abs(reference))` per channel. The 600,000 by 256 capture must complete within four seconds and use at most 24 MiB peak resident memory, measured by the driver.

items.command:
/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
import math, subprocess
from public_check import sample

def check(n, w):
    ref = [0.0] * 8
    for start in range(n - w + 1):
        for c in range(8):
            ref[c] += sum(sample(i, c) for i in range(start, start + w)) / w
    p = subprocess.run(['./probe', str(n), str(w)], text=True, capture_output=True, check=True)
    got = list(map(float, p.stdout.split()))
    assert len(got) == 8 and all(math.isfinite(x) for x in got)
    assert all(abs(a-b) <= max(.02, 2e-7*abs(b)) for a,b in zip(got, ref)), (n,w,got,ref)
    print(f'PASS boundary oracle n={n} w={w}')

for shape in [(1,1),(257,1),(257,256),(257,257)]:
    check(*shape)
for args in [('./probe','0','1'),('./probe','2','0'),('./probe','2','3'),('./probe','600001','1'),('./probe','1x','1')]:
    p = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True)
    assert p.returncode == 2, (args, p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr)
print('PASS invalid CLI inputs (5 cases)')
PY"
